ac2e2e1c91a51e0c.title: Evaluation of object detection neural networks to find topologically associated domains in bulk Hi-C data
digest: Topologically associated domains (TADs) shape the three-dimensional structure of chromatin and contribute to gene regulation by arranging regulatory elements and genes in spatial proximity.
This spatial proximity is captured by Hi-C, an experimental method, which quantifies contact frequencies between all pairs of genomic loci.
In bulk Hi-C data, TADs can be found in the form of gapped, nested and partially overlapping squares centered on the main diagonal of the Hi-C matrix.

digest: Exercise reduces all-cause mortality, yet its molecular effects across organs, sexes, and circadian phases remain incompletely understood.

We subjected mice to 8 weeks of voluntary wheel running and collected 22 tissues and plasma during active and inactive phases for bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, proteomics, and single-nucleus RNA and methylation sequencing.
Except for the hypothalamus, kidney, and lung, most tissues changed more during the active phase.

digest: HER2-directed therapy is unestablished in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and spatial HER2 heterogeneity remains poorly characterized.
Through nation-wide reflex HER2 testing, 62 patients (7.7%) met conventional HER2-positive criteria among 806 screened patients.
The pri-mary endpoint six-month progression-free survival rate was 46.7% (95% confidence interval, 21.3-73.4%); six of 11 patients with measurable disease achieved a partial response.
